applyTo: "rcsc/player/denoise_logger.*,rcsc/player/player_agent.*,rcsc/player/player_config.*"

# Denoise Dataset Logger (`rcsc::DenoiseLogger`) - Data Dictionary

## TL;DR

Per-agent dataset logger for training observation denoisers: every agent writes raw sensors, librcsc estimates, server ground truth, commands and a behavior label each cycle (`DenoiseLogger::SCHEMA_VERSION` = 2, also in `meta.json`).

- Enable with `--denoise_log_dir DIR` (empty = logger is not even created). Truth needs `--use_fullstate false --debug_fullstate true` (helios: `start.sh --fullstate reference --denoise-log-dir DIR`).
- Output: `<denoise_log_dir>/<game_id>/<side>_<unum>/` with `agent_cycle`, `objects`, `landmarks`, `hear`, `extra_tracks`, `raw_stream` (`.csv.gz`, or plain `.csv` when built without zlib) and `meta.json`.
- All coordinates are in the GLOBAL server frame (left team frame), angles in degrees, missing value = empty field (never 0).
- Precomputed noise columns `n_* = observed - truth` (schema v2) are defined in "Noise columns"; the `*_err_*` columns are librcsc error BOUNDS, not real errors.
- Read-only: the logger only reads `WorldModel`, sensors, `ActionEffector`; it never changes the noisy world model.
- **Open the full file when:** you need a column meaning, a matching rule, or the frame convention.

## Noise columns (`n_*`, schema version 2)

Precomputed `noise = observed - truth`, so a user can average them without recomputing.

- Definition and sign: `n_X = observed X - true X`, signed. Vectors give `_dx`, `_dy` (global left-team frame, like all other columns) and `_d` = Euclidean norm of the difference. `n_*_d` is non-negative; `n_trk_heard_*_d` and the hear `n_player_*` columns have only the norm.
- Angles: the difference is normalized to [-180, 180) (`norm180`). Absolute angles are compared in the global frame, relative angles in the observer's own face frame (not flipped).
- Units: as the source columns (m, m/cycle, degrees, deg/cycle). `n_dist_rel = n_dist / true_dist` (empty if `true_dist` < 1e-6). 6 decimals.
- `n_est_pos_*` need `posValid()`, `n_est_vel_*` need `velValid()`, `n_est_body` and `n_est_face` need `faceValid()` (body and face share it); `n_est_neck`/`n_est_stamina` have no validity flag and are written whenever truth exists.
- Empty rule: empty if the observed value is missing/invalid (flag 0, invalid vector, no see/sense_body/localization this cycle, unknown angle) OR the truth is missing (`truth_valid=0`, object not on field, zero speed for a direction). A number is never derived from an invalid value. Truth is the fullstate of the SAME cycle (never back-filled).
- The existing `*_err_*` columns are librcsc's error BOUNDS, not real errors; they are kept.

| Column(s) | Observed - truth |
|---|---|
| T1 `n_est_pos_*`, `n_est_vel_*` | `est_pos`/`est_vel` - `tru_pos`/`tru_vel` |
| T1 `n_est_body`, `n_est_neck`, `n_est_face`, `n_est_stamina` | `est_body` - `tru_body`; `est_neck` - `tru_neck`; `est_face` - (`tru_body`+`tru_neck`); `est_stamina` - `tru_stamina` |
| T1 `n_rawfix_pos_*`, `n_rawfix_face` | raw self fix vs `tru_pos`, vs `tru_body`+`tru_neck` (only if the fix is of this cycle) |
| T1 `n_sb_speed_mag` | `sb_speed_mag` - \|`tru_vel`\| (server quantizes the magnitude to 0.01) |
| T1 `n_sb_speed_dir` | `sb_speed_dir` - (direction of `tru_vel` - (`tru_body`+`tru_neck`)); empty if the true speed is ~0. Same convention as the server sense_body |
| T1 `n_sb_neck`, `n_sb_stamina` | `sb_neck_dir` - `tru_neck`; `sb_stamina` - `tru_stamina` |
| T2 `n_dist`, `n_dir` | raw `dist`/`dir` - `true_dist`/`true_dir` |
| T2 `n_dist_chg`, `n_dir_chg` | raw `dist_chg`/`dir_chg` - `true_dch`/`true_dirch` (only if the velocity was seen) |
| T2 `n_body_rel`, `n_head_rel` | raw `body_rel`/`head_rel` - (obj body - own body - own neck) / (obj body + obj neck - own body - own neck), true values (players only, only if the raw field exists) |
| T2 `n_ls_rpos_*`, `n_ls_pos_*`, `n_ls_vel_*`, `n_ls_rvel_*` | localized see vs (`tru_pos` - own `tru_pos`), `tru_pos`, `tru_vel`, (`tru_vel` - own `tru_vel`). `n_ls_rvel_*` is ball only (players have no `ls_rvel`) |
| T2 `n_trk_pos_*`, `n_trk_vel_*`, `n_trk_body`, `n_trk_face` | fused WM track vs truth (`n_trk_body/face` players only) |
| T2 `n_trk_heard_pos_d`, `n_trk_heard_vel_d` | heard pos/vel stored in the track vs truth (vel: ball only) |
| T3 `n_dist`, `n_dist_rel`, `n_dir` | raw landmark `dist`/`dir` - `true_dist`/`true_dir` (flags/goals with a known position; lines and behind markers are skipped) |
| T4 `n_ball_*`, `n_goalie_*`, `n_player_*` | decoded teammate payload vs the truth of this cycle. Only if the message time is the current cycle. The content may describe the sender's world of an earlier cycle, so it includes aging, not only sensor noise |

Server conventions (rcssserver): `body_rel`/`head_rel` = `normalize(obj_body [+ obj_neck] - self_body - self_neck)` (`visualsenderplayer.h` calcBodyDir/calcHeadDir, values truncated to int); sense_body speed dir = `int(normalize(vel.th - body - neck))`, magnitude quantized to 0.01 (`bodysender.cpp`); `dist_chg`/`dir_chg` are the radial and tangential (deg) relative velocity (`visualsenderplayer.cpp`).

## Where the code is

- `rcsc/player/denoise_logger.h/.cpp` - the logger (pimpl). Column lists are the `COLS_*` constants at the top of the .cpp.
- Hooks in `rcsc/player/player_agent.cpp`: `initImpl` (create), `parse` (`onReceive`), `Impl::sendRaw` (`onSend`, replaces every `M_client->sendMessage`), `action()` (`beginCycle` right after `updateJustBeforeDecision`; `preSend` just BEFORE `ActionEffector::makeCommand()`, which deletes the queued command objects; `endCycle` after the command batch is sent and before `clearAllCommands`), `finalize` (`close`), `~PlayerAgent` (`close()` + `reset()` of the logger while all members are alive).
- `PlayerAgent::addActionLabel( label )` (public) forwards to the logger. helios-base calls it in `SamplePlayer::actionImpl/doPreprocess` and `Bhv_PlannedAction::execute`.
- Lifecycle: `M_impl` (which owns the logger) is declared before the world model and effector, so it is destroyed after them. Therefore `~PlayerAgent` calls `close()` and resets the logger first; `close()` is idempotent; `~DenoiseLogger` never touches the owner agent (it only closes the files if `close()` was not called).
- Write-only WM records (never read by WM logic; valid only if their time equals the current `GameTime`): raw self fix `WorldModel::selfRaw*()` (written in `localizeSelf`); ball see localization `WorldModel::seeBallRecord()` (`SeeBallRecord`, filled in `localizeBall`); player see localizations `seePlayerRecordTime()` / `seePlayerRecords()` (`SeePlayerRecord`, filled by `addSeePlayerRecord` in `localizePlayers`, aligned with the raw `VisualSensor` entry by list kind 0=opponents 1=unknownOpponents 2=teammates 3=unknownTeammates 4=unknownPlayers + index in that list). They are reset in `updateAfterSee` before localization, so "flags false" means that this see produced no localization. Self raw fix: see above. Truth: `PlayerAgent::fullstateSensor()` (parsed in `analyzeFullstate` even if `debug_fullstate` is false).
- Options (`PlayerConfig`): `denoise_log_dir` (empty = off), `denoise_game_id` (empty = `<timestamp>_<own team>[_vs_<their team>]`, which can differ between agents - pass one explicit id, `start.sh` does), `denoise_log_landmarks` (default true), `denoise_log_raw` (default true).

## Conventions (all tables)

- Keys on every row: `game_id, side (l|r), unum, cycle, stopped`. `cycle` = agent time at the snapshot (hear rows: snapshot cycle, original in `hear_cycle`; raw stream rows: cycle of the message header).
- Object id: 0 = ball, 1-11 = left unum, 12-22 = right unum (global side, not team-relative).
- Frame: WorldModel, localization results and the fullstate sensor are in the team-normalized frame (`reverseSide`: the right team gets x,y negated and body angles +180). The logger un-reverses them when `ourSide == RIGHT`: positions/velocities/relative vectors `x,y -> -x,-y`; global angles (`*_body`, `*_face`, `angle_from_self`) `+180` normalized to (-180,180]. NOT flipped: raw see `dist/dir`, `*_rel` angles, `neck`, `focus_dir`, `pointto` angles, sense_body values, `true_dir` (relative to the true face).
- `ObjectTable::landmarkMap()` and the marker ids of the see parser are already global (the WM reverses after localization), so `land_x/land_y` are NOT flipped.
- Limitation: the WM uses `is_reverse_side()` (world_model.cpp) which differs from `ourSide` only in penalty shootouts; shootout data is not guaranteed consistent.
- Numbers: 4 decimals; 6 decimals for `true_*`/`tru_pos/vel/body/neck`/`match_err_deg` (noise free mode) and all `n_*` noise columns. Booleans 0/1. Strings are CSV-escaped (CR/LF flattened to a space), except the raw stream `msg` (reversible escape, see T6).
- Truth is never back-filled: if the fullstate of a cycle arrives late (not at the cycle of the decision), `truth_valid=0` for that row and the truth columns stay empty.
- Error handling: after every write/flush the stream state is checked. On the first failure the logger reports once to stderr, stops logging, closes the files and writes `meta.json` with `"status": "error"` and `"error"` (best effort). The periodic flush (every 50 cycles) is NOT crash-safe: a killed process can lose the end of the gz streams (and the gz trailer); only a clean `close()` guarantees complete files. `Table::close()` closes the concrete stream explicitly (`gzofstream::close()` / `ofstream::close()`) and checks `good()` after the close; `gzfilebuf::close()` returns failure if the last flush or `gzclose()` failed, which sets failbit in `gzofstream::close()`.
- `move_x/move_y` are the sent team-frame values multiplied by the side (as the server does), i.e. global.

## T1 `agent_cycle` (1 row per decision cycle, 155 columns)

Skipped cycles: if a new decision cycle follows the last row by more than 1 cycle in the same `stopped == 0` stream (the agent missed decisions), `beginCycle` first writes one PLACEHOLDER row per missing cycle (at most 6000 per jump) with the keys and `decision_made=0`; every other column is empty and no `objects` rows exist for them. Real rows have `decision_made=1`. Late truth is not back-filled into placeholders.

## T2 `objects` (ball + 21 other players per logged cycle, 134 columns)

All 22 rows (ids 0..22 except this agent) are ALWAYS written for each real T1 row. If `truth_valid=0`, the `tru_*`, `true_*`, `tru_on_field`, `in_cone`, `within_visible_dist` and `match_err_deg` columns are empty; unum matches of the raw see and WM tracks still fill the other columns (nearest-dir / nearest-position matching needs the truth, so those entries are not matched).

| noise | `n_dist`, `n_dist_rel`, `n_dir`, `n_dist_chg`, `n_dir_chg`, `n_body_rel`, `n_head_rel`, `n_ls_rpos_dx`, `n_ls_rpos_dy`, `n_ls_rpos_d`, `n_ls_pos_dx`, `n_ls_pos_dy`, `n_ls_pos_d`, `n_ls_vel_dx`, `n_ls_vel_dy`, `n_ls_vel_d`, `n_ls_rvel_dx`, `n_ls_rvel_dy`, `n_ls_rvel_d`, `n_trk_pos_dx`, `n_trk_pos_dy`, `n_trk_pos_d`, `n_trk_vel_dx`, `n_trk_vel_dy`, `n_trk_vel_d`, `n_trk_body`, `n_trk_face`, `n_trk_heard_pos_d`, `n_trk_heard_vel_d` | Observed - truth per object, see "Noise columns". |
| match | `match_method, match_err_deg, match_ambiguous, raw_dup_dropped` | How the raw see player was assigned to the truth id (see Matching). |
| localized see | `ls_valid, ls_rel_valid, ls_pos_valid, ls_vel_valid, ls_rvel_valid, ls_pos_*, ls_pos_err_*, ls_vel_*, ls_vel_err_*, ls_vel_count, ls_rpos_*, ls_rpos_err_*, ls_rvel_*, ls_rvel_err_*, ls_dist_error` | Localization result of THIS cycle's see (before fusion), taken from the write-only WM records (not inferred from `*Count()`), only written if a see arrived this cycle. `ls_valid=1` if the record of this see exists (ball: at least one of rpos/pos/vel computed; player: the raw entry was localized), `0` if the see was received but not localized (e.g. face/self pos invalid). `ls_rel_valid` relative position, `ls_pos_valid` global position, `ls_vel_valid` global velocity, `ls_rvel_valid` relative velocity (ball) were computed; each group of columns is empty if its flag is 0. Ball: all groups, errors are absolute (`ls_pos_err` = self pos error + rpos error; the rel pos is kept even if self pos is invalid); `ls_vel_count` = librcsc velocity quality (0 = from see velocity, larger = estimated by position difference). Players (looked up by the matched raw entry, not by the track): `ls_rpos_*`, `ls_pos_*`, `ls_vel_*` (may be empty) and `ls_dist_error`. All vectors global (un-reversed). |
| WM track | `track_found, track_match, track_match_dist, trk_*` | The fused world-model object matched to this truth id. Counts are librcsc age counters (0 = fresh). `trk_pos_err/vel_err` ball only. `trk_heard_vel_*` ball only. The ball initializes its heard pos/vel to (0,0) with count 1000 (never heard), so the ball `trk_heard_pos_x/y`, `trk_heard_vel_x/y` and `n_trk_heard_*_d` are written only if the matching `heardPosCount()`/`heardVelCount()` is < 1000 (counts saturate at 1000, so a very old heard value is empty too); players init heard pos as invalid, so the vector validity is enough. |

## T3 `landmarks` (one row per seen flag/goal/line, if `denoise_log_landmarks`)

Columns: `landmark_name`, `landmark_id`, `kind`, `dist`, `dir`, `dist_chg`, `dir_chg`, `land_x`, `land_y`, `true_dist`, `true_dir`, `true_focus_dist`, `n_dist`, `n_dist_rel`, `n_dir`.

`kind`: `flag|goal|behind_flag|behind_goal|line`. `landmark_name` from the `MarkerID` enum order (`Goal_L`, `Flag_C`, ...), `behind`/`Line_*` for others; `landmark_id` = `MarkerID` value (empty for behind markers and lines). `dist/dir` raw; `dist_chg/dir_chg` are always empty (the parser does not keep them). `land_x/y` global field position. `true_*` from the true own state (empty for lines and behind markers). `n_dist/n_dist_rel/n_dir` = raw see - truth (same rows; lines are skipped because the server line distance/direction convention is not modelled).

## T4 `hear` (one row per `hear` from self/teammates/opponents; referee/coach rows only in raw_stream)

Columns: `hear_cycle`, `sender_kind`, `sender_side`, `sender_unum`, `hear_dir`, `has_content`, `raw_msg`, `decoded`, `sender_true_x`, `sender_true_y`, `sender_true_dist`, `sender_true_dir_rel`, `n_ball_pos_dx`, `n_ball_pos_dy`, `n_ball_pos_d`, `n_ball_vel_dx`, `n_ball_vel_dy`, `n_ball_vel_d`, `n_goalie_pos_dx`, `n_goalie_pos_dy`, `n_goalie_pos_d`, `n_player_n`, `n_player_pos_d_mean`, `n_player_pos_d_max`.

`sender_kind`: `self|teammate|opponent|teammate_partial|opponent_partial` (partial = message not received, e.g. too many). `hear_dir` raw relative direction (empty for self/partial). `raw_msg` as sent. `decoded` = summary of `AudioMemory` items of the same time and sender (`ball(x y vx vy);pass(...);player(...)...`, global frame). `sender_true_*` only for known own-team senders. `n_*` = decoded payload of a TEAMMATE message - truth of this cycle (see "Noise columns"); the table has no per-row target, so the payload is matched by item type: `n_ball_*` (ball item), `n_goalie_*` (goalie item = opponent goalie), `n_player_*` (player items: count, mean and max position error; unum 1-11 own team, 12-22 opponent).

## T5 `extra_tracks` (WM tracks that were not matched to a truth id)

Columns: `track_list`, `trk_side`, `trk_unum`, `pos_x`, `pos_y`, `vel_x`, `vel_y`, `body`, `face`, `pos_count`, `vel_count`, `body_count`, `face_count`, `is_ghost`, `dist_from_self`, `angle_from_self`, `reason`.

`reason`: `no_truth`, `dup_unum` (second track with the same unum; the lower `posCount` is kept), `is_self`, `bad_unum`, `unmatched` (no free truth within 5 m / side-incompatible), `no_pos`. `track_list`: `teammate|opponent|unknown`.

## T6 `raw_stream` (if `denoise_log_raw`)

Columns: `local_ms`, `dir`, `msg`.

Every received (`recv`) and sent (`send`) message. The `msg` field is escaped reversibly: `\` -> `\\`, LF -> `\n`, CR -> `\r`, NUL dropped (then CSV-quoted if it contains `,` or `"`). Decode: parse the CSV, then replace `\\n`, `\\r`, `\\\\` left to right (a single regex `\\(.)` mapping `n`->LF, `r`->CR, `\\`->`\`). `local_ms` is the local epoch time in ms. Messages before the side/unum is known are buffered (max 4000) and written when the files are opened.

## Matching rules

- Raw see player with unum: id by (side, unum), `match_method=unum`.
- Raw see player without unum: among truth ids not claimed by unum entries (same side if the team is visible), the smallest |dir - true_dir| (tie: |dist - true_dist|), `match_method=nearest_dir`; `match_ambiguous=1` if the second best is within 1.0 deg. Close `(P)` form and low-quality `(p dir)` players are not kept by the parser, so they never appear.
- Duplicates on one id: unum match beats nearest_dir, then the smaller error wins; the rest is counted in `raw_dup_dropped` / `see_n_unmatched`.
- WM tracks: known unum -> id directly (`track_match=unum`); unknown unum -> greedy nearest truth within 5 m and side-compatible (`track_match=nearest`); the rest goes to `extra_tracks`.
- These are heuristics for labeling; use `match_err_deg`, `match_ambiguous` and `track_match_dist` to filter.

## `meta.json`

`schema_version`, `game_id`, `created`, `final` (false at the first snapshot; `true` only if `close()` flushed and explicitly closed every table - `gzclose`/`close()` status checked - and then wrote `meta.json` successfully, together with `status: "ok"`; any failure gives `final: false`, `status: "error"`), `status` (`ok` or `error`) and, on error, `error` (message of the first write failure), `side`, `unum`, `goalie`, team names, `last_cycle`, scores, frame/units/decimals, `compressed`, `config` (version, `gaussian_see`, `use_fullstate`, `debug_fullstate`, `synch_see`, logger flags, `full_view`, `see_noise_free`), `player_type_id`, `tables` (column lists), `player_types` (all heterogeneous types incl. noise rates) and the full `server_param` / `player_param` dumps (string values).

## Caveats

- If `use_fullstate` is true (default) the WM itself is built from truth; the logger still works but estimates equal truth. Use reference mode for training data.
- Verified by reading code only; not compiled or run when written. Missed decisions are represented by placeholder rows (`decision_made=0`) only within one `stopped == 0` stream; gaps across `stopped != 0` rows or beyond the 6000-row cap are not filled.
- Column names in the `Row` builders are checked at runtime: an unknown name prints one `(DenoiseLogger) unknown column name` warning.
